subject.title: Exec/tool failures show "(see attached image)" and suppress model response

question: Should exec-like read-only failures with no delivered user reply surface a compact warning, the generic incomplete-turn fallback, or a new recovery-aware terminal state?
rationale: Current source shows both warning suppression and incomplete-turn suppression are intentional enough to be covered by tests, and adjacent issues cover privacy and retry-confirmation policy; automation should not choose the permanent channel-visible contract alone.

options.title: Adopt a unified terminal-error contract
options.body: Show a channel-safe compact warning or incomplete-turn fallback when no user reply was delivered, while preserving suppression for acknowledged, recovered, or already-delivered failures.

options.title: Keep current suppression defaults
options.body: Leave read-only exec-like failures quiet unless verbose or cron/heartbeat detail policy applies, accepting that this issue remains unresolved for no-reply channel turns.

options.title: Split into narrower canonical issues
options.body: Let the open image-placeholder PR handle media downgrade only and route warning/fallback semantics to the broader tool-failure policy issue.

recommendation.title: Adopt a unified terminal-error contract
recommendation.body: Show a channel-safe compact warning or incomplete-turn fallback when no user reply was delivered, while preserving suppression for acknowledged, recovered, or already-delivered failures.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans terminal-classifier, provider replay, and policy-sensitive channel output behavior, and steipete has the strongest recent history across those boundaries.
